name: Slow Cooker Maple & Dijon Pot Roast
equipment: Slow cooker, Dutch oven or heavy skillet

items: 2½ to 3 lb beef chuck roast (see Recipe Notes)
4 to 5 slices bacon, diced (or neutral cooking oil)
3 large onions, peeled and sliced into half moons
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps.title: Season the meat
steps.body: Pat the pork dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Render the bacon
steps.body: Set a large Dutch oven or heavy skillet over medium-high to high heat. Add **4 to 5 slices bacon**, diced, and cook until some fat starts rendering and it begins to turn golden.

steps.title: Sear the beef
steps.body: Push the bacon to the sides and add **2½ to 3 lb beef chuck roast**. Sear both sides until golden brown, about 10 minutes per side, and transfer all the meat to the bowl of the slow cooker.

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.body: Pour off all but **2 Tbsp** of the bacon fat. Reduce heat to medium. Add **3 large onions**, peeled and sliced into half moons, and cook until starting to soften, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Deglaze the pan
steps.body: Pour in a few tablespoons of chicken stock and bring to a boil, scraping up any of the brown bits from the bottom of the pan. Pour the onions and pan juices into the bowl of the slow cooker.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.body: In a separate bowl, whisk the remaining chicken stock, **1 Tbsp Dijon mustard**, **1 Tbsp balsamic vinegar**, **1 Tbsp maple syrup**, **1 tsp paprika**, **1 tsp kosher salt**, and pepper until combined. Pour the liquid mixture over the roast.

steps.title: Slow cook
steps.body: Close the lid and cook on LOW heat until the meat falls apart and is meltingly tender, about 8 hours.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.body: Transfer the roast to a serving bowl or platter and cover with foil. Pour the cooking liquids into a large saucepan and bring to a boil. Cook until the gravy is reduced to desired thickness.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Cut the roast into chunks and pour hot gravy over the top. Serve with creamy grits, egg noodles, or mashed potatoes and/or oven-roasted carrots.
